content.text:
The drawing is a PROTAC-like molecule. I read it region by region, left to right.

**Pyridazine end.** The ring is a pyridazine with two adjacent nitrogens. One ring carbon next to N carries NH2. The next carbon carries the O-CH2 ether. The ring CH follows, then the carbon bearing the 2-hydroxyphenyl group, which sits next to the other N. As SMILES: Nc1nnc(-c2ccccc2O)cc1OC...

**Bicyclo[1.1.1]pentane.** The CH2 from the ether attaches to a bridgehead carbon (C1). The other bridgehead (C3) carries the C(=O)N amide. Three CH2 bridges link the two bridgeheads: C12(CC1(C2)...) works as the pattern.

**Linker.** The amide N is followed by CH2CH2, then O, then azetidine C3. The azetidine nitrogen is attached to the aromatic ring of the isoindoline-1,3-dione. The glutarimide (2,6-dioxopiperidin-3-yl) is on the imide N. No stereo is drawn.

**Isoindoline-dione.** The azetidine is attached at position 5 of the ring. In the drawing, the aromatic carbon bearing the azetidine N is the lower left, meta to the carbonyl-bearing ring fusion carbon at the bottom, and para to the upper fusion carbon.

SMILES: Nc1nnc(-c2ccccc2O)cc1OCC13CC(C1)(C3)C(=O)NCCOC1CN(C1)c1ccc2C(=O)N(C3CCC(=O)NC3=O)C(=O)c2c1

Checking the bicyclopentane SMILES: C13CC(C1)(C3)... opens ring 1 and ring 3 at the first atom. CC(C1)(C3): the C after C13 is a CH2 bridge to the second bridgehead. Then (C1) is a CH2 that closes to the first bridgehead, and (C3) is another CH2 that closes ring 3. So the second bridgehead has three CH2 bridges plus the amide carbon, which is correct.

The aromatic ring: c1ccc2C(=O)N(...)C(=O)c2c1. The atom c1 is attached to the azetidine N, followed by c, c, and c2, which is the fusion carbon bearing C(=O). After the imide, c2 closes the other fusion carbon, and the final c1 is the CH between that fusion carbon and the substituted carbon. The substituent is therefore adjacent to a CH that is adjacent to a fusion carbon, which is position 5. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: Nc1nnc(-c2ccccc2O)cc1OCC13CC(C1)(C3)C(=O)NCCOC1CN(C1)c1ccc2C(=O)N(C3CCC(=O)NC3=O)C(=O)c2c1
